intro: A handful of muruku gives about 160 kcal (estimate). Most of the calories come from rice flour and the oil absorbed while frying.
diet: Yes, one handful of muruku won't ruin your progress. The thing is, muruku is crunchy and salty, so it's very easy to go for a second and third handful. It's low in protein, so it doesn't keep you full. Treat it as an enjoy-sometimes snack, not a daily one.
tips: Take one handful and put it on a small plate. Don't eat straight from the jar.
During Deepavali or open houses, pick just 1-2 types of kuih and enjoy slowly.
Pair with protein like a boiled egg or nuts so you feel fuller.

swap.name: Homemade air-popped popcorn, 3 cups
swap.why: Still crunchy and salty, but bigger volume with fewer calories.

faq.a: Muruku is usually made from rice flour and urad dal flour, mixed with sesame or cumin, shaped into coils and fried.
In an airtight container, muruku usually stays crispy for a few weeks. Keep it away from humid air so it doesn't go lemau.

faq.q: Can muruku be made in an air fryer?
faq.a: Some people make muruku in the air fryer or oven to cut down oil. It's less crispy than fried, but lower in calories.
